judgementCalls.question: Does a proven-inert slippage guard, whose failure irreversibly consumes a caller's stablecoin, satisfy the C4 High limb 'assets can be stolen/lost/compromised directly (or indirectly if there is a valid attack path that does not have hand-wavy hypotheticals)'?
judgementCalls.verdict: MEDIUM - High declined. This is the run's decisive call and the reasoning is recorded in full so a reader can disagree with it on the merits.
theCaseForHigh: Real user assets are irreversibly lost: the stablecoin is pulled at :246 and deposited into the yield strategy through a minter that exposes no redeem, burn or withdraw path (verified by grep at HEAD, zero hits).

There is not one hypothetical in the mechanism. Halmos proves `totalPhUSD < minPhUSDOut` unsatisfiable over minPhUSDOut in [0, amount] on an UNBOUNDED domain at both 6- and 18-decimal profiles, with four required-fail falsifiability controls confirming the harness observes reverts rather than pruning them.
C4's High limb reads 'stolen/LOST/compromised'. Loss without theft can be High; the absence of a beneficiary is not by itself disqualifying.
The user who triggers it is not making a mistake. Stating minPhUSDOut = amount is the natural computation, and it is silently equivalent to stating zero.
theCaseForMedium_ANDWHYITWINS: (1) THERE IS NO ATTACKER, AND C4's HIGH LIMB IS WRITTEN AROUND ONE. No party receives the caller's stablecoin (it goes to the protocol's own yield strategy), no party can create the triggering condition (updateExchangeRate is onlyOwner in a nested dependency), and no permissionless action moves the protocol into the loss state. What this is, precisely, is a MISSING PROTECTION that fails to defend against an ordinary configuration - which is the exact shape C4's Medium limb is worded for: 'leak value with a hypothetical attack path with stated assumptions, but external requirements'. That wording fits this finding better than any paraphrase of it could.

(2) THE EXTERNAL REQUIREMENT IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS NOT SATISFIED BY DEFAULT. At parity (R == 1e18) the shortfall is exactly zero and this finding has no impact at all. Every unit of loss is gated on an owner rate movement below parity that the caller neither triggers nor observes. Presenting the 40% worked figure as an unconditional outcome would overstate it, and overstatement is a documented failure mode of this pipeline.

(3) PART OF THE NOMINAL SHORTFALL IS NOT ECONOMIC LOSS. The exchange rate exists, on the owner's own recorded triage, 'in case of a depeg'. Where R tracks a genuine depeg, delivering 160 phUSD for 100 antimatter plus 100 units of a $0.60 stablecoin is correct pricing, not theft. The honest residual - and it is a real one - is confined to stale, mis-set and zero rates.
whatWasREFUSEDInTheOtherDirection: REFUSED: dismissing it as a caller footgun. The caller who states the natural non-zero floor is EXERCISING the protection, not declining it. 'The caller passed a bad parameter' is true only of minPhUSDOut == 0 and is false across the rest of the band.

REFUSED: the yield-funded-pot opportunity-cost carve-out. That carve-out covers over-payment out of externally-derived yield on protocol-owned capital. Here a real stablecoin leaves a user's balance and cannot be recovered. It is a loss, and it falls on a user.

INV-A proves nothing reverts post-burn over this band. A promise-to-fix whose reasoning has since been falsified is the OPPOSITE of a disposal and carries no suppression authority.

The configuration that triggers the loss is the configuration the owner was told was safe, and the incompleteness was baked into the AGREED FIX PLAN rather than introduced by the executor - so this is not a rare corner nobody considered, it is a corner that was considered and waved through on refuted arithmetic. judgementCalls.question: Does caller-chosen, quantity-based stablecoin pairing against a manually-maintained rate with no staleness bound reach the C4 Medium limb 'leak value with stated assumptions and external requirements'?
judgementCalls.verdict: LOW - HELD. Medium declined on a marginal-capability test established from source at this stage.
judgementCalls.reasoning: The Medium limb is engaged on its face and I am not pretending otherwise: phUSD minted against collateral worth less than its registered rate is unbacked, which this project's own precedent treats as real dilution rather than opportunity cost. It is declined for two reasons, the first decisive. (1) MARGINAL CAPABILITY IS ZERO. PhusdStableMinter.mint (PhusdStableMinter.sol:203) is `external nonReentrant` with NO access control - verified at this stage by reading the nested source and enumerating its onlyOwner surface, which covers registerStablecoin, updateExchangeRate, setStablecoinEnabled, approveYS and setMaxMintPerDay and none of the user functions. Anyone holding the depegged stable can mint phUSD directly against the stale rate, without antimatter, in strictly larger size than the annihilate path allows (which is additionally bounded by the actor's antimatter balance). Attributing the dilution to Antimatter would credit it with a capability it does not add, and the root cause - the absent staleness bound - lives in a nested dependency outside first-party scope (parked MR-03-D-08). (2) THE CONJUNCTION IS ASSERTED, NOT OBSERVED: it needs a real depeg AND unresolved owner latency AND at least two registered stables to choose between, and none of the three is established at HEAD. What genuinely survives as first-party is the operational asymmetry - the caller's asset selection is unconstrained, so the latency window on a manual rate is adversarially selected against rather than merely exposed. That is an operational-hazard Low.

entries.label: L-03
entries.verdict: ENDORSED - low -> medium, with a binding no-double-count instruction
entries.reasoning: It was Low as a denial of service: the call reverted, funds were safe, the function was unavailable for that pair. That is no longer what it is. With the protocol-side zero guard deleted, at R == 0 the annihilation SETTLES - the caller's whole stablecoin half is consumed into the yield strategy with no redeem path, only the antimatter half is delivered, and Annihilated is emitted as if normal. An availability failure has been traded for a silent, irreversible, 100% value failure on the same lines, and the trade was made by deleting a guard rather than by making anything safe. That reaches the C4 Medium limb on the same wording as M-07 ('leak value with stated assumptions and external requirements'), and it is additionally a textbook non-obvious owner footgun in the Law-3 sense: an owner who sets a rate to zero would reasonably expect to be DISABLING that stable, and would be surprised to learn it silently confiscates annihilators' stablecoins instead. Medium is also the ceiling - no attacker, no permissionless trigger, and the R == 0 configuration is narrow.

findings.c4Criterion: Medium (2) - 'leak value with a hypothetical attack path with stated assumptions, but external requirements'. The value leak is real, demonstrated and irreversible; it is gated on an external requirement (a live exchange rate below parity) that no attacker can create, that the caller does not control, and that arises from an ordinary, sanctioned owner operation rather than from an attack.

classification.assetImpact: USER assets, not protocol assets. A caller who annihilates while the registered exchange rate R is below parity surrenders `amount` (18-dec) of a real stablecoin, pulled at :246 and deposited irreversibly into the yield strategy through PhusdStableMinter.mint, and receives amount + amount*R/1e18 phUSD instead of 2*amount. The stablecoin cannot be recovered: PhusdStableMinter exposes no redeem, burn or withdraw entry point (verified by grep at 3a96fb7, zero hits), and Antimatter holds no residue (StableNotDeposited at :255 asserts the balance returned to its pre-call value). BINDING (ADJ-02): the protocol balance sheet strictly IMPROVES at every R < 1e18. This must never be written up as a protocol value leak.
attackPath: 0. PRECONDITION (external, not attacker-created): the owner has set the registered exchangeRate for `stable` below 1e18. PhusdStableMinter.updateExchangeRate is onlyOwner (PhusdStableMinter.sol:138) and exists precisely so the owner can re-price a depegged stable - it is an ordinary operational act.

1. Alice holds 100e18 antimatter and 100e6 USDC. She reads the NatSpec at :222-225, which tells her minPhUSDOut is 'the least phUSD the caller will accept in total, counting both halves' and that passing zero waives the protection.

2. She reasons in the natural units of the trade: the antimatter half is fixed at `amount`, so the only leg that can move is the stable half. She sets minPhUSDOut = 100e18 - i.e. 'at worst give me back what my antimatter alone is worth'. This is a NON-ZERO floor and she believes she is protected.
3. annihilate burns her 100e18 antimatter at :239 (irreversible, effects-first) and pulls her 100e6 USDC at :246.
4. At R = 6e17 the minter mints 60e18 phUSD for the stable half. :259 computes totalPhUSD = 100e18 + 60e18 = 160e18.
5. :260 evaluates `160e18 < 100e18` -> false. The floor does not fire. The call SETTLES.

6. Alice receives 160e18 phUSD against the 200e18 the documented 2x property promises - a 40e18 (20% of total, 40% of the stable leg) shortfall - and the Annihilated event at :266 emits totalPhUSD as if normal, with minPhUSDOut appearing nowhere in the event, so no on-chain record exists that a floor was ever stated.

7. At the R = 0 endpoint the same path delivers only the antimatter half and the entire stablecoin is consumed for nothing (that endpoint is carried separately by ledger 0ed1c6e3270816c5 / L-03, whose mitigation is orthogonal).

GENERALISATION (proven, not extrapolated): step 5 holds for EVERY minPhUSDOut in [0, amount] and every R. Halmos check_invA_d18 and check_invA_d06 both PASS over an unbounded domain (amount, minPhUSDOut, R all full uint256), so `totalPhUSD < minPhUSDOut` is unsatisfiable throughout that band. The useful range of the guard begins one wei above `amount`.
classification.likelihood: MODERATE, and higher than the fix record implies. It needs no attacker, no race and no unusual caller behaviour - only (a) R below parity at execution time and (b) a caller who states a floor at or below the antimatter half. (b) is the natural choice, not a mistake: the antimatter half is the only figure the caller knows exactly, `amount` is the only quantity in the signature to anchor on, and the NatSpec presents ZERO as THE opt-out without ever saying that [1, amount] waives identically. The project's own suite reinforces the error - all six floor tests use values strictly above `amount`, so no test in the repository demonstrates the inert band. (a) is the ordinary operating state the owner was told was safe: F-01's human triageReason sanctioned deleting the protocol-side zero guard on the premise that 'a post-burn revert unwinds the whole transaction anyway', a premise Halmos INV-A now refutes over exactly this band.
assumptions: The registered exchangeRate R for the chosen stable is below 1e18 at the moment the transaction lands. At R == 1e18 (parity) there is no shortfall at all and this finding has no impact.
The caller states a floor in [0, amount] rather than strictly above `amount`.

The caller values the stablecoin they surrender at more than R per unit - i.e. the rate is stale, mis-set, or set to zero. Where R correctly reflects a genuine depeg the nominal shortfall is a correct re-pricing and the caller's ECONOMIC loss is smaller than the 40% nominal figure. The severity is carried on the mis-set / stale / zero cases, and this qualification must survive into the write-up.
classification.externalRequirements: An owner rate movement below parity, via PhusdStableMinter.updateExchangeRate (onlyOwner, in a nested read-only dependency). No attacker can create this condition and no attacker profits from it: the surrendered stablecoin goes to the yield strategy, not to a counterparty. There is no theft, no sandwich and no permissionless trigger.

findings.justification: MEDIUM, and the High/Medium line is where this finding actually turns, so the reasoning is recorded rather than asserted. The case FOR High is not weak: real user assets are irreversibly lost, the mechanism carries no hypotheticals whatsoever (Halmos proves the guard unsatisfiable over [0, amount] on an unbounded domain, with four required-fail falsifiability controls confirming the harness observes reverts rather than pruning them), and C4's High limb reads 'stolen/LOST/compromised' - loss without theft can be High. Three things hold it at Medium, and they are properties of the C4 text, not of a wish to keep the report tidy. FIRST, there is no attack path in the C4 sense, because there is no attacker: no party gains the caller's stablecoin, no party can create the triggering condition, and no permissionless action moves the protocol into the loss state. The loss is a MISSING PROTECTION that fails to defend against an ordinary configuration, which is precisely the shape C4 places at Medium and precisely why its Medium limb is worded as 'leak value ... with stated assumptions, but external requirements' rather than as an attack. SECOND, the external requirement is load-bearing and is not satisfied at HEAD by default: at parity the shortfall is exactly zero, so the loss is gated on an owner action in a nested dependency that the caller neither triggers nor observes. Reporting the 40% figure as an unconditional outcome would overstate it. THIRD, part of the nominal shortfall is not economic loss at all - where R tracks a genuine depeg, paying 160 phUSD for 100 antimatter plus 100 units of a $0.60 stablecoin is correct pricing, and the honest residual is confined to stale, mis-set and zero rates. Set against that, this must NOT be understated either, and three specific temptations are refused: it is not dismissible as a caller footgun (the caller who states the natural non-zero floor is exercising the protection, not declining it), it is not dismissible under the yield-funded-pot opportunity-cost carve-out (a real stablecoin leaves the caller's balance and cannot be recovered), and it is not dismissible on the story's own acceptance record (that record's stated ground - 'standard minOut == 0 DeFi behaviour, a protection the caller opted out of' - is refuted by the proof, since [1, amount] waives exactly as completely as 0). Medium is the honest band: the protocol's function is impaired in the specific sense that the only protection annihilate offers its callers does not work over the half of its domain callers will naturally use.
